transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-08-12 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Laura (MediCore Head of Platform), Daniel (Security), Priya (SRE), Mike (PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a roughly 30 to 45 minute walkthrough — show the console, org and project keys, how rate limits are applied, and then Riley will take us into some of the technical plumbing. Feel free to hop in.

[00:18] Laura: Great thanks. Quick context — we're evaluating vendors for model inference across our clinical routing product. Main things: per-tenant isolation, ability to set per-project quotas, and strong auditability. We have HIPAA-ish controls and need to map to internal policies.

[00:35] Riley: Awesome. I can show how Redwood handles org vs project keys: org keys are top-level and can be scoped to projects; projects get individual keys and quota profiles.

[01:10] Mike: When you say quota profiles, is that per-second QPS or per-month token budgets? We need both — bursts for real-time triage routes and monthly budgets for cost control.

[01:28] Samir: Good Q. We support rate limits (requests per second), concurrent request limits, and token-based quotas for billing windows. You can combine them: e.g., project A gets 50 QPS with 2M token monthly cap, project B is 10 QPS.

[02:05] Daniel: Security question up front — do audit logs capture API key usage per-project and do you surface KMS key ids for encryption at rest? We need to keep cryptographic controls in our ticketing system.

[02:20] Riley: Logs are per-token/key and per-request; all events are exportable to your SIEM. For KMS, in Private we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) — hosted also supports envelope encryption with dedicated KMS options. I'll show the console controls in a sec.

[03:10] [screen share starts]
Riley: Okay, console — top left is org settings. Under security > API keys you can create org keys or project keys. Here I'm going to create a project key for "triage-service". When you create a key you can select a quota profile or create a custom one.

[04:02] Riley: Note: Keys can be rotating automatically, and we offer short-lived tokens for ephemeral services. There's also an RBAC layer so you can limit who can create keys.

[05:15] Priya: Can we bind a key to a VPC or IP allowlist? We need network-level restrictions.

[05:25] Riley: Yes, for Private/dedicated you can restrict by VPC or by CIDR allowlists. For hosted we offer IP allowlists and OAuth-based token exchange integrations. (small audio skip)

[06:10] Samir: Let's switch to rate-limits policy. In this org we have a global policy and override rules per project. You can do rate-limit tiers (gold/silver) and also route-based limits. For example you might want a higher QPS for low-latency streaming endpoints and stricter quotas for batch jobs.

[07:00] Laura: How are bursts handled? Our triage endpoint gets sudden spikes during peak hours, we'd like throttling but graceful degradation not hard 429s always.

[07:20] Riley: Redwood supports token-bucket style bursting and weighted routing — you can set a burst window and fallback model variants. We also support queueing with timeouts so requests either queue or fallback to a cheaper/smaller model.

[08:12] Daniel: Any observability on cost — like per-project token spend and per-route latency? We want to tie spend back to feature teams.

[08:30] Samir: Yes, the console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and you can set alert thresholds. We'll also show Optimize suggestions — it recommends batching or quantization profiles when it detects high unit cost.

[09:00] Riley: Quick demo of quotas: I'll set a monthly token cap for "triage-service" to 2,000,000 tokens and show what happens when it's near limit — you can choose soft-stop with alerts or hard cutoff.

[10:05] [typo in auto transcript: "triage-server" vs "triage-service"]

[11:00] Mike: If a project hits a hard cutoff, do we have a queue or is it immediate 429? We need a way to gracefully degrade to cached responses.

[11:18] Riley: You can configure fallback routes — e.g., direct to cached responses or to a cheaper model. There's also a feature for pre-warming cache on predictable routes.

[12:30] Laura: Can we set per-user or per-tenant limits inside our project? Our customers (clinics) also have different SLAs.

[12:45] Samir: Two approaches: create sub-projects per-tenant (recommended for strict isolation), or use project-level tenant tagging with per-tenant quota enforcement through rules. Sub-projects are cleaner for billing and audit.

[14:00] Daniel: On compliance — SOC 2, ISO, data residency. Do you have SOC 2 Type II? How long are audit logs retained and can we push to our SIEM?

[14:18] Samir: We are SOC 2 Type II certified; logs retention is configurable, and you can export raw logs to S3 or to your SIEM via streaming. For Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem.

[15:05] Priya: How about SSO — can we map roles so only certain engineers can create keys or change quotas?

[15:20] Riley: Yes we integrate with SAML/SSO, and you can map groups to roles: admin, billing, operator, viewer. You can also set MFA requirements.

[16:05] [Riley opens network/security doc link in chat: https://redwood.example/security/keys-guide]

[16:40] Riley: Now a quick look at policy rules engine — you can write allow/deny rules, rate-limiting rules, and attach them to projects. It's a simple DSL in the UI, or you can upload JSON policies via API.

[17:45] Laura: Is the DSL audited? We need to know who changed a rule and when.

[17:55] Riley: Yes, policy changes are logged with user and timestamp; rollbacks are available.

[18:30] Samir: Moving on to the API — creating a request with a project key automatically enforces that project's limits. We'll show an example curl and then a small Node snippet.

[19:05] Riley: Example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <project_key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -d '{"model":"openredwood-35b","input":"..."}'  (note: demo snippet simplified)

[20:20] Mike: You mentioned per-route limits, how do we define a route? Path-based or header-based?

[20:35] Riley: Configurable — most customers use path + method. You can also set tagging rules based on headers to treat certain traffic differently.

[21:50] Daniel: For hosted offering, where are the regions? We have EU residency requirements for some customers.

[22:05] Samir: We have hosted regions in US-West, US-East, and EU-West. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in your region.

[23:10] Priya: If we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, do keys and configs migrate smoothly?

[23:30] Riley: Yes, config and policy objects are portable; keys can be reissued. There's a migration playbook we share.

[24:05] [screen: Optimize tab]
Riley: Here's Optimize — it analyzes your traffic and suggests batching, quantization, and model variants to reduce tokens/cost. For rate-limited endpoints it flags opportunities to raise throughput via batching.

[25:00] Laura: Can Optimize simulate projected costs if we change a quota?

[25:12] Riley: It gives cost estimates and impact on latency; it's an analysis not a guarantee.

[26:30] Samir: Quick rebuttal of competitor question — some vendors don't expose per-project token breakdowns or fine-grained policy defaults; Redwood's console is aimed at that multi-tenant visibility.

[27:15] Mike: Any limits on number of projects or keys? We run hundreds of tenants.

[27:30] Riley: No hard limits for enterprise; for hosted very large scale we recommend Dedicated tier.

[28:10] [brief crosstalk]

[29:00] Daniel: We want to test a sandbox. Is there a way to get a test org and generate sandbox keys?

[29:15] Samir: Yes we will spin up a test org with sandbox keys and pre-configured quota profiles. We'll include sample data and routes for benchmarking.

[30:05] Priya: Network — for private we need IP allowlist and VPC peering notes. We'll want to schedule that technical call so Riley can bring network diagrams.

[30:25] Riley: I'll prepare the diagram and a checklist of required firewall rules.

[31:00] [minor audio artifact — transcript shows "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"]

[32:10] Laura: Pricing question — are quota overages billed or blocked? How do you handle burst credits?

[32:25] Samir: You can opt for soft alerts (notify and allow with overage billing) or hard cutoffs. For enterprise we can do committed usage contracts with burst allowances.

[33:40] Mike: If we want dedicated capacity for predictable latency, what does on-boarding look like? Lead times?

[33:55] Riley: Dedicated usually has a 4–8 week lead time depending on capacity and region. We do capacity planning with your expected QPS and model footprint.

[35:10] Daniel: For encryption keys, if we use our KMS, do you store any plaintext?

[35:22] Riley: No plaintext storage. Envelope encryption used; you control KMS keys and we store only ciphertext. We can provide a diagram.

[36:15] [Samir shares pricing doc link in chat: https://redwood.example/pricing/dedicated]

[36:40] Laura: One last technical: how are rate limits enforced in the runtime? Do you use a central proxy or local per-node enforcement? Concerned about single points of failure.

[36:55] Riley: Enforcement is runtime-distributed: a smart routing layer admits requests and nodes enforce local quotas with global counters using a lease-based sync. It's designed to avoid central throttles as single points of failure. (small pause) There are edge cases with clock skew but we mitigate with conservative leases.

[38:20] Priya: Sounds good. Next steps recap?

[38:30] Samir: Recap: we'll send pricing + security whitepaper, Riley will schedule a technical deep dive focused on network and private deployment, and we'll provision a sandbox org with keys for benchmarking. Customer to share QPS/route list.

[39:05] Laura: That works. Also please include the policy DSL examples and audit log retention options in the email.

[39:20] Samir: Will do. Anything else?

[39:30] Mike: No, thanks — appreciate the detailed demo.

[40:00] [wrap up small chat]

Notes about transcript quality: automated captions had a few mis-hearings (KV cache -> KV cash, triage-service spelled inconsistently). Links shared: security guide and pricing doc in chat.

End of meeting.
